patches.SOURCE_ANCHOR: She appears throughout her show at City Art Gallery in self-portraits, often with her young son.
patches.WHY_GROUNDED: The source names the venue City Art Gallery; City Art Centre appears nowhere in it. Restores the correct proper noun, which the article itself uses earlier.

patches.OLD_TEXT: a person who did not know the work existed an hour ago
patches.NEW_TEXT: a person who may never have heard of the work
patches.SOURCE_ANCHOR: You can’t walk into a gallery without learning about some subcultural genius or longlost creative you’ve never heard of.
patches.WHY_GROUNDED: The source supports only possible unfamiliarity (‘never heard of’); it gives no timeline and no settled knowledge-state. The invented one-hour interval is removed and the assertion softened to the source's own modality.

patches.OLD_TEXT: and the second side is the one that presses
patches.NEW_TEXT: and the second side, on the reading offered here, is the one that presses
patches.SOURCE_ANCHOR: I think they have a duty – to viewers and to their subjects – to tell them clearly.
patches.WHY_GROUNDED: The source names both directions of the duty but never weighs them against each other. The comparative is marked as the article's own interpretation rather than something the review established.
